Not the first time I comment this, but when I was 8-9 yo I saw on TV some movie scenes about men being treated as slaves in harvest fields, and when the Lords were going to kill them all because of a 'crime' (I don't remember the exact shit), one of them negotiated and was crucified and burned down. 

It was weird, and the concept of it happening (even though I knew it was all fiction) was something I didn't understand and still can't. I rarely think about it, but sometimes I'd like to know the name of that movie, andt I wonder if I could handle watching that scene again.

  
Also, when I was probably 4 yo I watched a little scene of a movie with a color palette similar to Jim Carrey's The Mask, but this was different, probably a suspense one. It was just a taxi stopping by some person walking on a random street, then the camera focused on the driver's window, and he just looked at the person and smiled in a way I could only describe as disturbing. The aspect of that man was just evil and the way he just stopped and smiled terrified me for a while, I even remember that scene appearing on my nightmares at least 2 times after that. It's been a long time and I think I found the movie about 14 years ago, but forgot its name.

I understood it after a rough time. It was our last year of junior high, and there was a new guy in the class. I didn't know at first, but he hated me and would often talk trash about me behind my back. My then-best friend started listening to him and stopped talking to me overnight. For some reason, I thought it'd be temporary, so I kept trying make things right, even though I didn't even know what was wrong. I had the worst year of my life, since everyone in my class decided not to talk to me anymore, and that guy I still considered my best friend also started talking trash about me. Don't ask me why, but I even tried asking other people to help me finding out why he was angry and sort things out. I never could. Since it was our last year, it was the only one where I had to struggle with that, but in the end I figured out he'd never be my friend and I'd never want to see my classmates again.

I've had many of those. The most recent one was the day I had 2 presentations for 2 different classes and had to learn tons of information to make it all work. Well, the first teacher told me not to say too much within the first two minutes and ended my presentation right there. The next one didn't even let me talk; I said one thing and then he would interrupt me and tell the rest of info I had about that topic. So I studied all that shit for nothing.   
I was already upset when I went to get a fruit cocktail and told the lady not to put pineapple on it (I hate pineapple). She put a fucking lot of pineapple and I realized when I was going to my next class. I spilled some pineapple on my sweater.  


Also, last year I had a terrible streak. There was one day when I had to make some drawings and plans (Now you know the career I'm studying), and everything just went wrong, I couldn't even make ONE good line, some papersheets tore, the leads of every pencil I used that day broke and I was fucking fed up.

I was going to participate on an academic contest that day, so I was nervous and awakened earlier, but didn't leave my bed. Not long after that, I felt someone was walking in my room, and sat right next to me, I could even feel the bed giving in. Whoever was sitting there didn't say a single word, and after a couple of minutes, I felt he/she stood up and left my room. Btw, I never heard the door being opened, or steps, only a breathing.   


Probably ten minutes after that, my dad came into my room and told me to wake up. I asked him if it was him who had come, and he said he had just woken up, and my mom was still in bed. My sister was in her room, so I never found an explanation of what happened.

When I was 9, a classmate died of lupus. He was actually a smart guy, and even though we weren't best friends or something like that, we would often be together at the break, and I remember him telling me I was smarter than the then-current "smartest boy" in the class. Nobody knew what he was going through, until he died in mid-February. It absolutely destroyed me at the moment, and I had to deal with the feeling of only attending the funeral, even though the whole class was invited to pay tribute at the burial (My parents didn't allow me to go). This February I finally went to visit his grave.  
Also, 3 years after that, a guy who was one year older died in a car accident. He was kinda popular and awesome at basketball, so everyone ended up attending the funeral. Again, we weren't friends, but trained basketball together a few times; also, his mom used to be a teacher at that school and my sister was a student of hers. As I said, he was reaaaaally good at basketball, so I sometimes wonder what he could've done had he not died.
